qa.q: Assertion (A): Many non-Assamese groups demanded separate states. Reason (R): They felt the Assamese language was being imposed on them.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Mizoram has remained in armed conflict ever since the 1986 accord. Reason (R): After the Mizoram Accord, Laldenga became Chief Minister.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: Mizoram has been largely peaceful since. R is true.

qa.q: Which organisation led the Assam Movement of 1979-1985?
qa.a: All Assam Students' Union
qa.e: AASU led the movement.

qa.q: The main demand of the Assam Movement was:
qa.a: Identification and deportation of illegal migrants
qa.e: It focused on 'outsiders', mainly from Bangladesh.

qa.q: The Assam Accord was signed in:
qa.e: It was signed in 1985 with the Rajiv Gandhi government.

qa.q: Which party was formed by AASU leaders after the Assam Accord?
qa.a: Asom Gana Parishad
qa.e: The AGP won the 1985 election.

qa.q: Who became Chief Minister of Assam in 1985 as leader of the AGP?
qa.a: Prafulla Kumar Mahanta
qa.e: Mahanta led the AGP government.

qa.q: Under the Assam Accord, migrants from which period were to be identified and deported?
qa.a: During and after the Bangladesh war (from 1971)
qa.e: The accord used 1971 as the key period.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Local communities in Assam opposed large-scale migration. Reason (R): They feared becoming a minority and losing jobs, land and political power.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The Assam Movement aimed at Assam's secession from India. Reason (R): The Assam Movement was led by the AASU.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: it focused on illegal migrants, not secession. R is true.

qa.q: According to the chapter, regional aspirations should be seen as:
qa.a: A part of democratic politics
qa.e: They are normal in a diverse democracy.

qa.q: The best way to respond to regional demands is through:
qa.a: Democratic negotiation
qa.e: Accords show the value of negotiation.

qa.q: Which constitutional arrangement provides autonomous councils for tribal areas?
qa.a: The Sixth Schedule
qa.e: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils.

qa.q: Why does regional economic imbalance matter?
qa.a: It can create feelings of discrimination among regions
qa.e: Balanced development reduces grievances.

qa.q: Which accord was signed with Laldenga?
qa.a: Mizoram Accord
qa.e: Rajiv Gandhi and Laldenga signed it in 1986.

qa.q: Which is an example of power sharing with a region?
qa.a: Former insurgents becoming part of an elected state government
qa.e: Laldenga becoming Chief Minister is an example.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Accords helped bring peace to Mizoram and Punjab. Reason (R): Democratic negotiation gave groups a stake in the political system.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): India's Constitution is too rigid to accommodate regional diversity. Reason (R): The Sixth Schedule provides autonomous councils for tribal areas.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the Constitution is flexible. R is true and shows this.

qa.q: Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated on:
qa.e: He was killed during the 1991 election campaign.

qa.q: Who became Prime Minister after the 1991 election?
qa.a: P.V. Narasimha Rao
qa.e: Narasimha Rao led the Congress government from 1991.

qa.q: Which Lok Sabha election is seen as marking the end of the 'Congress system' of Congress dominance at the Centre?
qa.e: In 1989 the Congress lost its majority and coalition politics began. In 1977 it had lost too, but it returned to power in 1980.

qa.q: The New Economic Policy began in:
qa.e: Economic reforms began in 1991.

qa.q: Which issue brought backward-caste politics to the centre stage in 1990?
qa.a: The Mandal issue
qa.e: Implementation of the Mandal report in 1990 was a turning point.

qa.q: What was a major result of these developments?
qa.a: Multi-party competition and coalition governments
qa.e: No single party could easily win a majority.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The 1990s saw the rise of coalition governments at the Centre. Reason (R): No single party could easily win a majority in the Lok Sabha.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The Congress won a clear majority on its own in 1989. Reason (R): The Congress had won a massive victory in 1984.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: it lost its majority in 1989. R is true.

qa.q: Who became Prime Minister as head of the National Front government in 1989?
qa.a: V.P. Singh
qa.e: V.P. Singh led the National Front government.

qa.q: The National Front government of 1989 was supported from outside by:
qa.a: The BJP and the Left Front
qa.e: Two ideologically opposite groups supported it from outside.

qa.q: The United Front governments of 1996-98 were supported from outside by:
qa.a: The Congress
qa.e: The Congress backed the United Front from outside.

qa.q: Which two leaders were United Front Prime Ministers?
qa.a: H.D. Deve Gowda and I.K. Gujral
qa.e: Deve Gowda (1996-97) and Gujral (1997-98) led the United Front.

qa.q: Which party was at the core of the National Front in 1989?
qa.a: Janata Dal
qa.e: The National Front was led by the Janata Dal with regional parties.

qa.q: Why did the National Front government fall?
qa.a: The BJP withdrew its support
qa.e: Loss of outside support brought it down.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Coalition governments in the 1990s were often unstable. Reason (R): They depended on support from parties that were not part of the government.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): I.K. Gujral headed the National Front government of 1989. Reason (R): I.K. Gujral was a United Front Prime Minister.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: V.P. Singh headed the 1989 government. R is true.

qa.q: Who was Prime Minister of the NDA government from 1998 to 2004?
qa.a: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
qa.e: Vajpayee led the NDA government.

qa.q: The UPA was led by which party?
qa.a: Congress
qa.e: The Congress led the United Progressive Alliance.

qa.q: Manmohan Singh was Prime Minister from:
qa.e: He headed the UPA for two terms.

qa.q: The NDA government lost a confidence vote and faced fresh elections in:
qa.e: It lost a confidence vote in 1999 and returned after the 1999 election.

qa.q: During which period were coalition governments the norm at the Centre?
qa.e: No single party won a majority on its own in this period.

qa.q: Alliances in the coalition era were often formed on the basis of:
qa.a: Pragmatic considerations rather than shared ideology
qa.e: Practical needs often mattered more than ideology.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Regional parties gained influence at the national level from 1989 to 2014. Reason (R): National parties needed their support to form coalition governments.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The UPA was led by the BJP. Reason (R): The UPA governed from 2004 to 2014.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the Congress led the UPA. R is true.

qa.q: What percentage of reservation for OBCs did the Mandal Commission recommend?
qa.e: It recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs.

qa.q: The Mandal Commission was set up by:
qa.a: The Janata Party government in 1978
qa.e: The Janata government set it up.

qa.q: Which government decided to implement the Mandal recommendation in 1990?
qa.a: The National Front government under V.P. Singh
qa.e: V.P. Singh's government acted in August 1990.

qa.q: In which case did the Supreme Court uphold OBC reservation in 1992?
qa.a: Indra Sawhney case
qa.e: The Indra Sawhney case upheld the decision.

qa.q: Who founded the Bahujan Samaj Party?
qa.a: Kanshi Ram
qa.e: Kanshi Ram founded the BSP in 1984.

qa.q: The BSP first came to power in Uttar Pradesh in:
qa.e: It came to power in 1995.

qa.q: Assertion (A): There were widespread protests in 1990. Reason (R): The government decided to implement 27 per cent reservation for OBCs in central government jobs.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; the decision triggered the protests.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The Supreme Court struck down OBC reservation in the Indra Sawhney case. Reason (R): The Mandal Commission recommended 27 per cent reservation for OBCs.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the Court upheld it. R is true.

qa.q: The three-domed structure at Ayodhya was demolished on:
qa.a: 6 December 1992
qa.e: It was demolished on 6 December 1992.

qa.q: The Supreme Court delivered its verdict in the Ayodhya case on:
qa.a: 9 November 2019
qa.e: A five-judge bench ruled on 9 November 2019.

qa.q: How many judges were on the Constitution Bench that gave the 2019 Ayodhya verdict?
qa.e: It was a five-judge Constitution Bench.

qa.q: Under the 2019 verdict, how much land elsewhere in Ayodhya was to be given for a mosque?
qa.a: 5 acres
qa.e: The court directed five acres be allotted.

qa.q: From where did L.K. Advani's Rath Yatra of 1990 begin?
qa.a: Somnath
qa.e: It set out from Somnath in Gujarat.

qa.q: Which statement best describes the response to the 2019 verdict?
qa.a: It was accepted peacefully across the country
qa.e: The peaceful acceptance showed the strength of the legal process.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The Ayodhya dispute was finally settled through the courts. Reason (R): A five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court gave a unanimous verdict in 2019.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The consecration of the Ram temple took place in 1992. Reason (R): The Supreme Court's verdict came in 2019.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: the consecration was in January 2024. R is true.

qa.q: In 2014, the BJP became the first party since which year to win a Lok Sabha majority on its own?
qa.e: The Congress had won a majority on its own in 1984.

qa.q: How many Lok Sabha seats did the BJP win on its own in 2014?
qa.e: The BJP won 282 seats in 2014 and 303 in 2019.

qa.q: How many Lok Sabha seats did the BJP win on its own in 2019?
qa.e: In 2019 the BJP won 303 seats.

qa.q: Which is part of the new consensus in Indian politics?
qa.a: Acceptance of the political and social claims of backward castes
qa.e: Most parties accept these claims.

qa.q: The new consensus includes an emphasis on:
qa.a: Pragmatic considerations rather than ideological positions
qa.e: Alliances are often formed on practical grounds.

qa.q: What does the consensus say about state-level parties?
qa.a: Their role in national governance is accepted
qa.e: State parties became key partners at the Centre.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Most major parties now support economic reforms. Reason (R): Agreement on new economic policies is part of the new consensus.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both true; the consensus on economic policy explains the broad support.

qa.q: By how many seats did the BJP's own tally rise from 2014 to 2019?
